verdict.purpose: The page's one argued sentence; 26px below 768px. One per page.

finding.purpose: Section heading stating a conclusion generated from the figures; 19px on mobile.

figure.purpose: Key values in the ruled figure strip; tabular numerals.

secondary.purpose: Figure labels and notes, definitions, link buttons, compact controls.

label.purpose: Table headers, tags, bridge details, usual-range captions; sentence case, never uppercase.

shadows.name: segment-lift
shadows.purpose: Selected segment of the compare control only.

shadows.name: popover
shadows.purpose: Truly floating layers such as listboxes. Panels never cast shadows.

motion.name: ease-settle
motion.purpose: Shared ease-out for every data-change transition.

motion.name: settle
motion.purpose: Content that re-renders with the period settles in.

motion.name: bridge-tween
motion.purpose: Profit bridge bars move to their new to-scale lengths.

motion.name: series-bars
motion.purpose: Bar series heights ease on change.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Removes settle and pulse animations and disables bridge transitions.

narrative.overview:
Every page makes one claim about the month in a plain sentence, and every panel below it proves that claim. A cool grey ground holds white panels separated by hairline rules. One PriyaFil deep teal marks what is good, selected or actionable. Red is reserved for money lost and bad standings, and amber for things to watch.

The density is that of a well-set financial report. Sentences lead, and figures follow in tabular Manrope. The page opens on a verdict sentence over one ruled strip of figures, never a tile grid. Section headings are findings, not category names. Charts are drawn to scale, reconcile on screen, and also exist as real tables.

Light and dark carry equal weight. The dark theme keeps every role on a blue-green-tinted near-black.
keyCharacteristics: Finding-led section headings generated from the figures
Ruled figure strip, never boxed tiles
One teal accent: good, selected, actionable
Colour always paired with words, sign and arrow, or a legend

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Teal means good, selected or actionable, and nothing else. No second decorative hue.

rules.name: The Red Is Money Lost Rule
rules.body: Red marks only losses, adverse moves and bad standings. A fall is red only when the fall hurts.

rules.name: The Never Colour Alone Rule
rules.body: Every tone carries words, a sign and an arrow, or a legend.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Every figure uses tabular numerals so columns align.

rules.name: The Sentence Case Rule
rules.body: Labels are short sentence-case Slate words; never uppercase or letter-spaced.

rules.name: The Hierarchy Over Uniformity Rule
rules.body: Verdict as open text, figures as a ruled strip, proofs as panels: three registers, never one repeated card.

rules.name: The Flat Panel Rule
rules.body: Panels never cast shadows; a shadow means a layer truly floats.

dos: Do lead each section with a finding generated from the figures (lib/narrative.ts).
Do use plain names for ledger heads (lib/labels.ts); only Statements keep Tally's names.
Do format every figure through lib/money.ts: ₹ Cr/L, one lakh precision per column, true minus, per-kg rates, no −0.0%.
Do label missing data and say which month a lagging figure comes from.
Do give every chart a text alternative and make bridge totals reconcile on screen.
Do colour a change by whether it helps the business, with a sign and an arrow.
donts: Don't build rows or grids of KPI tiles.
Don't add eyebrow or kicker labels, or uppercase letter-spaced labels.
Don't add decorative sparklines, trend icons or background charts.
Don't use red beyond losses, adverse moves and bad standings, and don't add a second accent, gradients, gradient text or glassmorphism.
Don't render missing data as zero or as a red dash.
Don't let one outlier month flatten a series; mark it unusual and clip it.
